chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the woman who dies, 'Who is most rightful to pray upon her?' He said: 'The husband.' I said, 'The husband is more rightful than the father, the brother, and the son?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: Prayer (specifically funeral prayer in this context)

ai.seo_question: Who has the right to lead the funeral prayer for a deceased woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi explicitly prioritizes the husband over the father, brother, and son in leading the funeral prayer for a woman, reflecting the Shia juristic view of the husband's primary role as the head of the household. This ruling underscores the legal hierarchy of kinship in ritual duties, distinguishing the marital bond's immediate authority from that of consanguineal relatives in the context of funeral rites.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about the woman who dies, ‘Who would be most rightful to pray Salaat upon her?’ Heasws said: ‘The husband’. I said, ‘The husband is more rightful than the father, and the brother, and the son?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma‘il ibn Marrar from Yunus from abu Basir from who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a deceased woman as to who is most deserving to perform Salah (prayer) for her. He (the Imam) said, ‘Her husband deserves the most to perform Salah (prayer) for her.’ I then asked, ‘Is he more deserving than her father, brother or son? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he is more deserving.’”
